verdict.rationale: Unreal ships its own 2D system, Paper 2D. It is documented as a sprite-based system for 2D and 2D/3D hybrid games, and it includes Tile Sets and Tile Maps for painting 2D levels. However, the sprite documentation cited is the UE4 4.27 page, and the current tilemap documentation carries an Experimental banner. Nothing in the evidence shows dedicated 2D physics, since Chaos Physics is described as general rigid-body and destruction simulation. Nothing shows 2D being treated as a first-class workflow rather than a 3D add-on. Missing for 10: dedicated 2D physics, evidence that the 2D tooling is production-ready rather than experimental, current-version sprite documentation, and independent corroboration that 2D is a first-class workflow.

support.subject: As a game developer, 2D is a first-class workflow — sprites, tilemaps, 2D physics — not a 3D afterthought

citations.quote: Paper 2D in Unreal Engine 4 (UE4) is a sprite-based system for creating 2D and 2D/3D hybrid games entirely within the editor.
Tile Sets and Tile Maps within Paper 2D, provide a quick and easy way to layout the framework or 'general layout' of your 2D levels.
